definition: Done quickly and without real interest or care, only because it is expected.
examples: The guard gave my bag a *perfunctory* glance and waved me through.
His apology was so *perfunctory* that it made things worse.
translation: fait pour la forme, expédié, machinal

definition: Talking a lot, especially about unimportant things.
examples: My *garrulous* neighbour kept me on the doorstep for half an hour.
He becomes *garrulous* after a glass or two of wine.

definition: Lacking the energy, competence or sense of responsibility to achieve anything.
examples: Her *feckless* brother has never held a job for more than a month.
The papers blamed a *feckless* government for the delays.

definition: Stupid or slow to understand; looking vacant (British).
examples: Don't just stand there looking *gormless* — give me a hand!
He gave me a *gormless* grin and carried on eating.

definition: Completely confused and unable to know what to do or say.
examples: I was totally *flummoxed* by the last question in the interview.
Even the engineers looked *flummoxed* when the screen went blank.

definition: Feeling or showing a gentle sadness, especially a longing for something past or out of reach.
examples: She gave a *wistful* smile as the train pulled out.
He grew *wistful* whenever anyone mentioned his student days in Rome.

definition: Silently bad-tempered and resentful; refusing to be pleasant.
examples: The teenager sat in *sullen* silence throughout dinner.
She answered with a *sullen* shrug.

definition: Dull, bleak and depressing.
examples: It was a *dreary* November afternoon, grey and wet.
He was stuck in a *dreary* job filling in forms all day.

definition: Looking exhausted and unwell, especially from worry, lack of sleep or suffering.
examples: He came out of the meeting pale and *haggard*.
After three nights at the hospital her face was *haggard* with worry.

definition: Hard but easily broken or cracked; figuratively, fragile, or sharp and lacking warmth.
examples: Old paper becomes yellow and *brittle*.
She gave a *brittle* laugh that fooled nobody.

definition: Having or showing sharp practical judgement, especially in business or about people.
examples: She is a *shrewd* judge of character.
Selling the house before the crash turned out to be a *shrewd* move.

definition: Rude, unfriendly and ungracious.
examples: It would be *churlish* to refuse such a generous offer.
He gave a *churlish* grunt instead of saying thank you.

definition: To become gradually smaller, fewer or weaker.
examples: Our savings had *dwindled* to almost nothing by the spring.
The crowd slowly *dwindled* as the rain got heavier.

definition: Clever at getting what you want, especially by tricks.
examples: The *wily* old politician outmanoeuvred all his rivals.
She was too *wily* to fall for such an obvious trap.

definition: To stand or wait around somewhere without any obvious purpose.
examples: A group of teenagers were *loitering* outside the station.
Don't *loiter* on the way home from school.

definition: Lacking good manners; rough and awkward in behaviour or speech.
examples: His *uncouth* table manners embarrassed the whole family.
She found the new neighbours loud and *uncouth*.

definition: To wait or stay hidden, especially in order to do something bad; (of danger or doubt) to exist unseen.
examples: Someone was *lurking* in the shadows by the garage.
Doubt still *lurked* at the back of her mind.
translation: se tapir, rôder, être à l'affût

definition: Untidy and not cared for, especially of hair or appearance.
examples: He turned up unshaven, with *unkempt* hair and a creased shirt.
The garden had grown wild and *unkempt* since the old man died.

definition: Careless, untidy or dirty in appearance or habits.
examples: The landlord complained about the tenants' *slovenly* habits.
It was a *slovenly* piece of work, full of spelling mistakes.

definition: To hide or move about secretly, out of cowardice or with bad intent.
examples: A fox was *skulking* behind the bins.
He *skulked* off to his room to avoid the washing-up.
translation: rôder furtivement, se cacher, se défiler

definition: Done carelessly, without attention to detail.
examples: The report was rejected because of its *slipshod* research.
I won't pay for such *slipshod* workmanship.

definition: To walk in a quiet, cautious or furtive way, especially sideways.
examples: A man *sidled* up to me and asked if I wanted to buy a watch.
She *sidled* past the sleeping guard.

definition: Looking dishonest or evasive, as if hiding something.
examples: A *shifty* man in a long coat was hanging about outside the bank.
He went all *shifty* when I asked where the money had gone.

definition: Having no energy or enthusiasm.
examples: The heat left everyone *listless* and irritable.
She picked at her food in a *listless* way and went to bed early.

definition: To become unsteady or weaker; to hesitate between choices.
examples: His voice *wavered* as he read the letter aloud.
She never *wavered* in her support for him.

definition: Showing regret or sorrow, often in a slightly humorous way.
examples: He gave a *rueful* smile and admitted he had been wrong.
"I should have listened to you," she said with a *rueful* laugh.

definition: To be visibly and continuously worried or anxious.
examples: Don't *fret* — we have plenty of time.
She *frets* about her exams for weeks beforehand.
translation: se tracasser, se faire du souci

definition: Showing dry, slightly mocking humour; (of a face) twisted in amused disappointment.
examples: She made a *wry* comment about the quality of the hotel coffee.
He looked at the bill with a *wry* smile.

definition: To think for a long time about things that make you sad, angry or worried.
examples: He sat *brooding* over the insult all evening.
There is no point *brooding* about what might have been.

definition: Too pleased with yourself or with what you have achieved.
examples: He had a *smug* look on his face after winning the argument.
I can't stand her *smug* little remarks about how well her children are doing.

definition: Speaking or spoken easily and smoothly, but without sincerity or real thought.
examples: The minister gave a *glib* answer that explained nothing.
He is a *glib* salesman who could sell sand in the desert.
translation: désinvolte, spécieux, qui a du bagou

definition: To show unpleasant satisfaction at your own success or someone else's failure.
examples: She couldn't resist *gloating* over her rival's defeat.
I don't want to *gloat*, but I did warn you.

definition: Rough and unfriendly in manner or voice, though not necessarily unkind.
examples: Beneath his *gruff* manner he is a kind man.
"Sit down," said a *gruff* voice from behind the desk.

definition: To speak about something with mocking contempt.
examples: Experts *scoffed* at the idea when it was first proposed.
"You, a chef?" he *scoffed*.

definition: Changing often and unpredictably, especially in loyalties or tastes.
examples: Fashion is *fickle*: what sells this year is forgotten the next.
The weather here is *fickle*, so bring a raincoat.

definition: Showing stubborn determination in spite of difficulties.
examples: Her *dogged* persistence finally got her an interview.
Through sheer *dogged* effort he finished the marathon.

definition: To look at someone in an angry, sullen way.
examples: He *glowered* at the waiter who had spilled the wine.
She sat *glowering* in the corner, refusing to speak.
translation: lancer un regard noir, fusiller du regard

definition: Loyal, reliable and hard-working, especially over a long time.
examples: She has been a *stalwart* supporter of the club for forty years.
He remained *stalwart* in his defence of his old friend.

definition: To burn slowly with smoke but no flame; to feel strong emotion without showing it openly.
examples: The bonfire was still *smouldering* the next morning.
Resentment *smouldered* between the two families for years.

definition: Quick and light in movement or in thought.
examples: Her *nimble* fingers flew across the keyboard.
You need a *nimble* mind to keep up with him in a debate.

definition: To be uncomfortably hot.
examples: Commuters *sweltered* in the packed underground.
We were *sweltering* in our winter coats.

definition: Tall and thin, with long limbs and slightly awkward movements.
examples: A *lanky* teenager unfolded himself from the back seat.
He was a *lanky* man who had to stoop under every doorway.

definition: (Of a person) big, strong and heavily built.
examples: Two *burly* bouncers stood at the door of the club.
A *burly* farmer lifted the sack as if it weighed nothing.

definition: To avoid someone or something deliberately and consistently.
examples: After the scandal she was *shunned* by her former friends.
He *shuns* publicity and rarely gives interviews.

definition: Attractive or charming in a fresh, innocent way.
examples: The child gave a *winsome* smile and was instantly forgiven.
The film relies too heavily on its *winsome* heroine.

definition: To avoid work or a duty that you ought to do.
examples: He never *shirks* his share of the housework.
You can't *shirk* your responsibilities for ever.
translation: se dérober à, esquiver, tirer au flanc

definition: Sad and lonely, as if abandoned; (of a hope) unlikely to succeed.
examples: A *forlorn* little dog was waiting outside the shop in the rain.
They searched all night in the *forlorn* hope of finding survivors.

definition: To crouch or shrink back in fear.
examples: The dog *cowered* under the table during the storm.
They *cowered* in the doorway as the shots rang out.
translation: se recroqueviller de peur, se tapir

definition: Threatening harm; full of menace or ill will.
examples: The cat gave me a *baleful* stare from the top of the wardrobe.
The scandal had a *baleful* influence on the whole party.

definition: Unwilling or reluctant to do something.
examples: I am *loath* to interfere, but someone has to say something.
She was *loath* to leave the warm kitchen.

definition: To prevent someone from doing what they want, or a plan from succeeding.
examples: The police *thwarted* an attempt to rob the bank.
Her ambitions were *thwarted* at every turn.

definition: Annoying and tiresome.
examples: Filling in the same form every month is an *irksome* chore.
He found the constant interruptions deeply *irksome*.

definition: To trick or deceive someone.
examples: Thousands of investors were *hoodwinked* into buying worthless shares.
Don't let him *hoodwink* you with his charm.

definition: (Of praise, thanks or apologies) excessive to the point of sounding insincere.
examples: The chairman introduced her with *fulsome* praise that made her blush.
He was *fulsome* in his apologies, but nobody believed him.

definition: Embarrassed because you have done something silly or wrong.
examples: He came back with a *sheepish* grin, having locked the keys in the car.
She looked *sheepish* when I caught her finishing the cake.

definition: To complain or express sadness about something.
examples: Farmers *bemoan* the lack of rain every summer.
He is always *bemoaning* the decline of good manners.

definition: Sentimental in an exaggerated, embarrassing way.
examples: The film's ending is *mawkish* and far too long.
He wrote her a *mawkish* poem about eternal love.
translation: mièvre, larmoyant, à l'eau de rose

definition: To make someone or something seem unimportant.
examples: He *belittles* her achievements in front of their friends.
I don't want to *belittle* the effort they made.

definition: Slow-moving, slow to react, lacking energy.
examples: I always feel *sluggish* after a heavy lunch.
Sales have been *sluggish* since the summer.

definition: To abandon someone or something; to give something up.
examples: He *forsook* a career in law to become a painter.
She felt that all her friends had *forsaken* her.

definition: Distant and cold in manner; unfriendly.
examples: I thought she was *standoffish* at first, but she is just shy.
The locals can seem *standoffish* until they get to know you.

definition: (Of eyes or a person) tired, unfocused and unable to see clearly.
examples: He peered at the alarm clock with *bleary* eyes.
We stumbled off the night flight, *bleary* and unwashed.
translation: aux yeux troubles, embrumé de fatigue

definition: To stop someone who is on their way somewhere, in order to talk to or attack them.
examples: I was *waylaid* by a neighbour on my way to the car.
Reporters were waiting to *waylay* her outside the court.

definition: Unpleasantly damp and cold.
examples: They kept the wine in a *dank* cellar that smelled of mould.
The tunnel was dark and *dank*.

definition: To criticise or scold someone severely.
examples: She *upbraided* him for arriving late yet again.
The coach *upbraided* the team for their lazy performance.

definition: Unpleasantly damp and sticky to the touch.
examples: His hands were cold and *clammy* with nerves.
The *clammy* air of the cave made her shiver.

definition: To provoke or annoy someone until they react.
examples: He was *goaded* into losing his temper.
The older boys kept *goading* him to jump.

definition: Soaked through with liquid.
examples: We took off our *sodden* shoes at the door.
The pitch was so *sodden* that the match was called off.

definition: Twisted, rough and knotty, especially with age.
examples: An old man with *gnarled* hands was mending a net.
The path winds between *gnarled* olive trees.

definition: To understand something difficult after much thought.
examples: I can't *fathom* why she turned the job down.
It took me years to *fathom* what he had meant.

definition: (Of cloth) thin and worn with age; (of an excuse or argument) weak from overuse.
examples: He wore the same *threadbare* jacket every winter.
That excuse is getting rather *threadbare*.

definition: To take something from someone with effort or force.
examples: He *wrested* the knife from his attacker's hand.
The rebels are trying to *wrest* control of the capital from the army.

definition: (Of skin) of an unhealthy pale yellowish colour.
examples: Months of night shifts had left him thin and *sallow*.
Her *sallow* skin looked almost grey under the strip lights.

definition: Pale and looking ill or tired; weak, faint.
examples: She gave a *wan* smile and said she was fine.
He looked *wan* and thin after his illness.

definition: To argue over the price of something.
examples: We *haggled* over the price of the rug for an hour.
In this market you are expected to *haggle*.

definition: Small, shrivelled and wrinkled with age.
examples: A *wizened* old woman was selling herbs at the gate.
He picked a *wizened* apple from the bottom of the bowl.

definition: To take part in an activity in a casual, not very serious, way.
examples: She *dabbles* in watercolours at weekends.
He *dabbled* in politics before going into business.

definition: Deprived of something; sad and lonely after a loss.
examples: The speech was completely *bereft* of new ideas.
She felt utterly *bereft* when her children left home.

definition: To search deeply inside something; to investigate thoroughly.
examples: She *delved* into her bag and pulled out a crumpled map.
The book *delves* into the family's hidden past.

definition: Wet, dirty and untidy.
examples: A *bedraggled* cat was sheltering under the car.
We arrived *bedraggled* and exhausted after hours in the storm.

definition: Filled with horror or shock.
examples: She was *aghast* at the size of the bill.
The audience looked on, *aghast*, as the stage collapsed.

definition: To search a place violently, leaving it in disorder, often in order to steal.
examples: Burglars had *ransacked* every room in the house.
I *ransacked* my desk looking for the passport.
translation: saccager, fouiller de fond en comble

definition: Away from the planned or expected course; out of position, crooked.
examples: Our holiday plans went *awry* when the airline went bust.
His tie was *awry* and his hair uncombed.

definition: To sharpen (a blade); to stimulate (an appetite or interest).
examples: The smell from the kitchen *whetted* my appetite.
The trailer has *whetted* everyone's curiosity.

definition: Not friendly or willing to take part; distant.
examples: He stayed *aloof* from office gossip.
Some found her cold and *aloof*; others, merely reserved.

definition: Difficult to move or manage because of size, shape or complexity.
examples: The sofa was too *unwieldy* to carry up the stairs.
The committee has grown into a large, *unwieldy* body.

definition: To cause great damage or harm; to inflict (revenge).
examples: The storm *wreaked* havoc along the coast.
He swore to *wreak* revenge on those who had betrayed him.

definition: Moving in a clumsy, ungraceful way.
examples: On land, the seal is slow and *ungainly*.
He ran with an *ungainly*, loping stride.

definition: To have a strong, persistent desire for something.
examples: After a month abroad I was *hankering* after a proper cup of tea.
He still *hankers* for the simplicity of village life.
translation: avoir très envie de, soupirer après

definition: Dirty, shabby and often connected with dishonest or immoral activities.
examples: They met in a *seedy* bar near the docks.
He ended up in a *seedy* hotel with stained carpets.

definition: To roll about in mud or water; to indulge in an emotion or situation.
examples: Hippos *wallow* in the mud to keep cool.
Stop *wallowing* in self-pity and do something about it.

definition: Unwilling to change because of tradition or convention.
examples: The profession is too *hidebound* to accept such a reform.
He dismissed the board as a group of *hidebound* old men.

definition: Treated badly by those in power and lacking the strength to resist.
examples: The novel gives a voice to the *downtrodden* workers of the mills.
She was tired of playing the *downtrodden* wife.

definition: To lie or relax in pleasant warmth; to enjoy approval or attention.
examples: Lizards were *basking* on the warm stones.
He *basked* in the admiration of his colleagues.

definition: Difficult to control; following a wilful or unpredictable course.
examples: She spent years worrying about her *wayward* son.
He brushed a *wayward* lock of hair out of his eyes.

definition: To use the hands clumsily while doing or looking for something.
examples: She *fumbled* in her pocket for the keys.
He *fumbled* with the buttons of his coat.

definition: Unexpected and unwelcome; improper.
examples: If nothing *untoward* happens, we should arrive by six.
He swore that nothing *untoward* had taken place between them.

definition: To persuade someone, or obtain something, by flattery and coaxing.
examples: She *wheedled* her father into lending her the car.
He managed to *wheedle* an invitation out of them.

definition: Direct and honest in manner and speech.
examples: She was *forthright* in her criticism of the plan.
I admire his *forthright* way of dealing with complaints.

definition: Determined to do things your own way, refusing advice.
examples: She was a *headstrong* child who hated being told what to do.
He is too *headstrong* to listen to his doctors.

definition: To talk at length about trivial things.
examples: He *prattled* on about his holiday for an hour.
The children *prattled* happily in the back seat.

definition: Cheerfully careless; showing a casual indifference that seems improper.
examples: He spoke with a *blithe* disregard for the facts.
She carried on in *blithe* ignorance of the trouble she had caused.

definition: To be filled with intense but unexpressed anger; (of a place) to be crowded and full of movement.
examples: She was *seething* with rage but said nothing.
The square *seethed* with tourists.

definition: Paying no attention; careless of consequences.
examples: *Heedless* of the danger, he ran back into the building.
She drove on, *heedless* of the warning signs.
translation: insouciant de, sans se soucier de

definition: Done, or doing things, too quickly and carelessly.
examples: The painting job was *slapdash*, with drips all over the floor.
He has a *slapdash* approach to paperwork.
translation: bâclé, fait à la va-vite, brouillon

definition: To bite or chew at something persistently; to cause constant worry.
examples: The dog was *gnawing* a bone under the table.
Guilt *gnawed* at him for weeks.

definition: Owing a duty or thanks to someone in return for a favour.
examples: I don't want to be *beholden* to anyone, so I'll pay my own way.
A newspaper should not be *beholden* to its advertisers.

definition: To become gradually weaker or less; (of the moon) to appear smaller each night.
examples: Public interest in the trial soon *waned*.
His influence has been *waning* since the election.

definition: Suddenly and strongly in love with, or attracted to, someone or something.
examples: He was *smitten* with her from the moment they met.
One visit to Lisbon and I was completely *smitten*.

definition: To crowd closely together, or curl up the body, for warmth or protection.
examples: We *huddled* around the fire to keep warm.
She sat *huddled* in a blanket on the sofa.
translation: se blottir, se serrer les uns contre les autres

definition: Unwilling to say anything about something; with lips pressed together in anger.
examples: The company remains *tight-lipped* about its plans.
She gave a *tight-lipped* nod and left the room.
